title: Bayesian discounting models with brms
text: TMB tier’s SLT-beta family brms equivalent. Two options cover ground: family = "beta" (default): brms’s beta likelihood identity link; mean function squished (1e-6, 1 - 1e-6), differentiable analog TMB clamp. Boundary responses (y exactly 0 1) handled boundary: default "squeeze" applies Smithson-Verkuilen transform (y(N-1) + 0.5)/N responses reports boundary count; "zoib" switches zero-one-inflated beta – statistically explicit boundary responding, changes estimand: k describes interior responses ; "error" refuses fit. family = "gaussian": matches fit_dd_tmb(family = "gaussian") wherever TMB mean clamp ([1e-6, 1 - 1e-6]) bind – everywhere except extreme decay underflow. validation harness posterior median log k lands within hundredths TMB MLE.

title: Scoring the 27-Item Monetary Choice Questionnaire
text: Monetary Choice Questionnaire (MCQ; Kirby, Petry & Bickel, 1999) widely used paper--pencil measure delay discounting. item asks respondent choose smaller reward available immediately larger reward available delay, example “prefer $54 today $55 117 days?” 27 items constructed implied indifference points sweep across wide range discount rates three reward magnitudes (small, medium, large). pattern choices person makes estimates discount rate k Mazur’s (1987) hyperbola, V = / (1 + k * D). Scoring MCQ hand tedious error-prone. beezdiscounting automates procedure described Kaplan et al. (2016), returning k overall magnitude, along consistency choice-proportion diagnostics need judge whether respondent’s pattern interpretable.

title: Scoring the 27-Item Monetary Choice Questionnaire
text: score_mcq27() expects long-format data one row per item per respondent exactly three columns: subjectid, questionid (1–27), response. package includes small example, mcq27, two respondents: Responses coded 0 person chose smaller, immediate reward 1 chose larger, delayed reward. respondent almost always takes immediate money steep discounter (large k); one waits larger reward shallow discounter (small k). 27 items discount rates bracket fixed Kirby design. can inspect lookup table directly: item belongs magnitude band (magnitude: small, medium, large) sits one nine indifference k ranks (k_rank), defined smaller-immediate amount (ss_amount), larger-delayed amount (ll_amount), delay days.

title: Scoring the 27-Item Monetary Choice Questionnaire
text: score_mcq27() returns one row per respondent: output carries three families columns: Discount rates. overall_k single discount rate best matches full set choices; small_k, medium_k, large_k estimated within magnitude band; geomean_k geometric mean three magnitude-specific rates. what: Why indifference points need a bounded error distribution
title: Modeling delay-discounting indifference points with bounded error distributions
text: delay-discounting task asks person trade smaller-sooner reward larger-later one across range delays. indifference point (IP) delay smaller-sooner amount feels equivalent later reward, expressed proportion later reward. construction IP lives closed interval [0, 1]: y = 1: person indifferent immediate amount equals full later reward (discounting). y = 0: immediate amount, however small, preferred (complete discounting). Real titration data pile ends, example data shipped package (data(dd_ip)) reproduce pattern: meaningful fraction observations sit exactly 0 1. single fact rules two error distributions people reach first: Gaussian / nonlinear least squares treats residuals unbounded homoscedastic. can predict IP 0 1, assumes noise size near bounds middle, never true proportion. Standard beta regression natural model proportion, density undefined exactly 0 1 (log-likelihood -\infty). Every boundary observation discarded nudged, biases fit. Scale-Location-Truncated beta (SLT-beta) distribution (Kim, Koffarnus & Franck, 2024; Kim, Kaplan, Koffarnus & Franck, 2025) keeps beta’s natural fit proportion data assigns finite probability endpoints, 0 1 modeled rather thrown away.

title: Modeling delay-discounting indifference points with bounded error distributions
text: Write mean IP delay D discounting function single rate k, using either Mazur’s hyperbola \mu = 1/(1 + kD) exponential \mu = e^{-kD}, let \phi precision parameter (larger \phi gives tighter spread around curve). shape parameters = \mu\phi b = (1-\mu)\phi, two fixed micro-constants s = 1{+}10^{-7} l = 10^{-8}, log-density observed IP y \[0,1] \log f(y \mid \mu, \phi) = \underbrace{\log\Gamma({+}b) - \log\Gamma() - \log\Gamma(b)}_{-\log B(,b)} + ({-}1)\log\!\big(\tfrac{y}{s}{+}l\big) + (b{-}1)\log\!\big(1 - \big(\tfrac{y}{s}{+}l\big)\big) - \log s - \log Z, truncation normalizer Z = \mathrm{pbeta}(\tfrac{1}{s}{+}l,\,,\,b) - \mathrm{pbeta}(l,\,,\,b). intuition microscopic stretch: data window y\[0,1] mapped just inside open interval ordinary beta density finite; kernel therefore never evaluated exactly 0 1. s\1 l\0 SLT-beta collapses ordinary beta. SLT-beta (solid) vs. ordinary beta (dashed). SLT-beta carries finite density y = 0 y = 1; ordinary beta diverges vanishes . variance beta \mu(1-\mu)/(\phi+1), SLT-beta automatically gives less noise near floor ceiling middle: heteroscedastic pattern real IP data actually show, exactly Gaussian model gets wrong.
code: slt_logpdf <- function(y, mu, phi, s = 1.0000001, l = 1e-8) {   a <- mu * phi; b <- (1 - mu) * phi   lgamma(a + b) - lgamma(a) - lgamma(b) +     (a - 1) * log(y / s + l) + (b - 1) * log(1 - (y / s + l)) -     log(s) - log(pbeta(1 / s + l, a, b) - pbeta(l, a, b)) } yy <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 400) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) for (p in list(c(mu = 0.5, phi = 4), c(mu = 0.15, phi = 6))) {   plot(yy, exp(slt_logpdf(yy, p["mu"], p["phi"])), type = "l", lwd = 2,        xlab = "indifference point", ylab = "density",        main = sprintf("mu = %.2f, phi = %g", p["mu"], p["phi"]))   lines(yy, dbeta(yy, p["mu"] * p["phi"], (1 - p["mu"]) * p["phi"]), lty = 2)   points(c(0, 1), exp(slt_logpdf(c(0, 1), p["mu"], p["phi"])), pch = 16) } par(op)

title: Modeling delay-discounting indifference points with bounded error distributions
text: package ships dd_ip, synthetic delay-discounting dataset (100 subjects across six delays, id, x (delay), y (indifference point) long format) reproduces boundary pattern real titration data. handful synthetic values fall just 1 clamped ceiling. Many observations sit exactly 0 1. Counting subjects least one boundary value, asking error models can even evaluate : Every subject boundary value lost ordinary beta regression retained SLT-beta. Fitting subject individually (estimating \log k \log\phi stay positive) comparing recovered rate nonlinear least squares confirms SLT-beta agrees NLS bulk subjects succeeds boundary subjects NLS-plus-beta model: caveat next section resolves: fit one subject time SLT-beta likelihood can occasionally run degenerate solution. person whose indifference points almost 0s 1s, fit near-zero precision places mass endpoints can score higher likelihood sensible discounting curve. fix fit people isolation.
code: data(dd_ip) dd_ip$id <- factor(dd_ip$id) dd_ip$y  <- pmin(dd_ip$y, 1)            # clamp a few synthetic values to the [0, 1] ceiling c(observations        = nrow(dd_ip),   subjects            = nlevels(dd_ip$id),   at_floor_or_ceiling = sum(dd_ip$y %in% c(0, 1))) #>        observations            subjects at_floor_or_ceiling  #>                 600                 100                 129 beta_logpdf <- function(y, mu, phi) {          # ordinary beta: -Inf at y in {0,1}   a <- mu * phi; b <- (1 - mu) * phi   lgamma(a + b) - lgamma(a) - lgamma(b) + (a - 1) * log(y) + (b - 1) * log(1 - y) } ids <- levels(dd_ip$id) yof <- function(i) dd_ip$y[dd_ip$id == i] bnd     <- vapply(ids, function(i) any(yof(i) %in% c(0, 1)), logical(1)) beta_ok <- vapply(ids, function(i) all(is.finite(beta_logpdf(yof(i), 0.5, 8))), logical(1)) slt_ok  <- vapply(ids, function(i) all(is.finite(slt_logpdf(yof(i), 0.5, 8))), logical(1)) data.frame(   subjects                       = length(ids),   with_boundary_IP               = sum(bnd),   evaluable_under_ordinary_beta  = sum(beta_ok),   evaluable_under_SLT_beta       = sum(slt_ok) ) #>   subjects with_boundary_IP evaluable_under_ordinary_beta #> 1      100               76                            24 #>   evaluable_under_SLT_beta #> 1                      100 fit_slt <- function(y, D) {                      # per-subject SLT MLE (log k, log phi)   nll <- function(th) {     mu <- pmin(pmax(1 / (1 + exp(th[1]) * D), 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)     v <- -sum(slt_logpdf(y, mu, exp(th[2]))); if (is.finite(v)) v else 1e10   }   o <- optim(c(log(0.01), log(8)), nll, control = list(reltol = 1e-11))   exp(o$par[1]) } nls_k <- function(y, D) {                        # multi-start NLS (single start is fragile)   for (st in c(exp(-10), 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1)) {     m <- tryCatch(nls(y ~ 1 / (1 + k * D), start = list(k = st)), error = function(e) NULL)     if (!is.null(m)) return(coef(m)[["k"]])   }   NA_real_ } xof <- function(i) dd_ip$x[dd_ip$id == i] k_slt <- vapply(ids, function(i) fit_slt(yof(i), xof(i)), numeric(1)) k_nls <- vapply(ids, function(i) nls_k(yof(i), xof(i)), numeric(1)) sprintf("cor(log k): SLT vs NLS = %.3f   |   median k: SLT = %.4f, NLS = %.4f",         cor(log(k_slt), log(k_nls), use = "complete.obs"),         median(k_slt), median(k_nls, na.rm = TRUE)) #> [1] "cor(log k): SLT vs NLS = 0.978   |   median k: SLT = 0.5328, NLS = 0.5038"

text: Generates binary choices either structural descriptive choice model. mode = "structural" (default) choices drawn structural model: P(LL) = plogis(beta0 + gamma * ((ll/ss) * D(k, delay) - 1)), k_i = exp(log_k_pop + sigma_u * u_i). mode = "descriptive" choices follow Young's (2018) correlated random-slope logistic model: subject receives per-subject slopes drawn bivariate normal mean theta covariance Sigma, P(LL) = plogis((theta[1] + b_i[1]) * log(ll/ss) + (theta[2] + b_i[2]) * log(delay + 1)). descriptive branch known-truth generator used recovery tests.

text: check_unsystematic() calc_aucs() now compute results per id. title: beezdiscounting (development version)
text: fit_dd_tmb(..., random_effects = k + s ~ 1) now fits per-subject random intercept Green-Myerson / Rachlin curvature s, jointly log k, covariance_structure = "pdSymm" (correlated) "pdDiag" (independent), family = "sltb" "gaussian". Per-subject s_i soft-clamped toward (0.05, 20) (C-infinity softplus map; see de-hang note ). VarCorr()/ranef()/summary() surface (k, s) covariance per-subject s. predict() level = "subject" uses subject’s estimated s_i; response-SD standardization uses population precision phi. simulate_dd_ip() gains sigma_s/rho_ks generate (log k, log s) bivariate-normal data recovery testing. per-subject s random effect now uses smooth (C-infinity) softplus soft clamp instead hard clamp, clamp-binding subject (e.g. -discounting step subject) converges instead hanging Laplace inner solve.

title: beezdiscounting (development version)
text: New fit_dd_brms(): Bayesian mixed-effects discounting via brms/Stan four TMB equations ("mazur", "exponential", "green-myerson", "rachlin"). family = "beta" (identity link differentiable squish) closest brms analog TMB SLT-beta; family = "gaussian" matches TMB gaussian likelihood wherever TMB mu clamp bind (everywhere except extreme decay underflow). Boundary responses handled via Smithson-Verkuilen squeezing (default), zero-one-inflated beta (boundary = "zoib"; changes estimand), refusal. New fit_dd_choice_brms(): structural trial-level choice model bernoulli("logit"), matching fit_dd_choice(mode = "structural"), including -subject designs log k via factors/factor_interaction/continuous_covariates (rank-deficient designs rejected sampling; gamma b0 stay population-level). New default_dd_priors() / default_dd_choice_priors(): inspectable defaults delay-unit-aware logk anchoring (centers k * median(delay) = 1). S3 methods mirror TMB tier’s contracts: exact 8-column tidy() table (NA statistic/p.value; estimates posterior medians report-space-transformed draws), glance() elpd_loo/looic MCMC diagnostics place AIC/BIC, confint() quantile credible intervals, predict(), ranef() per-subject k posterior summaries indifference-point fits, print()/summary(). get_dd_param_emms() get_dd_comparisons() accept brms indifference-point structural choice fits: draws-based marginal means contrasts reference grid TMB path, quantile credible intervals post.prob (posterior probability direction) place adjusted p-values. init = "tmb" available Bayesian fitters (quiet TMB pre-fit supplies chain starting values, prior-center fallback). brms, posterior, loo Suggests-. New vignette “Comparing discounting rates groups” (vignette("dd-group-comparisons")): factor designs log k, estimated marginal means, contrasts across backends – TMB (Wald + holm) brms (posterior draws + post.prob) – indifference-point trial-level choice models alike.

title: beezdiscounting 0.4.0
text: New fit_dd_choice(mode = "structural") fits trial-level smaller-sooner vs larger-later choice binomial GLMM, estimating discount rate k directly (scale-invariant value comparison, optional choice-bias intercept). shares get_dd_param_emms()/get_dd_comparisons() k contract fit_dd_tmb() validated IP-vs-choice tie-. simulate_dd_choice() generates structural choice data. (Descriptive Young-2018 model: forthcoming.) New mcq27_to_choice() reshapes long-form 27-item Monetary Choice Questionnaire responses (subjectid/questionid/response) per-trial id/ss_amount/ll_amount/delay/choice frame consumed fit_dd_choice(), using canonical Kirby, Petry, & Bickel (1999) item design. get_lookup_table() now returns complete design (adds ss_amount, ll_amount, delay). fit_dd_tmb() simulate_dd_ip() gain two-parameter hyperboloid equations "green-myerson" (mu = (1 + k*x)^(-s)) "rachlin" (mu = 1 / (1 + k*x^s)), single population nonlinearity exponent s (reported tidy()/summary()/confint()). reduce "mazur" s = 1. Mixed-effects discounting via TMB (fit_dd_tmb()): fits indifference-point (IP) family discounting model — Mazur hyperbolic exponential mean subject random intercept log k — either scale-location-truncated beta (family = "sltb", default) Gaussian (family = "gaussian") observation family. -subject factors continuous covariates enter log k fixed-effect design. SLT-beta error distribution: assigns finite probability indifference points exactly 0 1, ordinary beta regression undefined. Means use identity link discounting function; variance shrinks near bounds grows mid-range. Estimated marginal means contrasts: get_dd_param_emms() returns EMM k per factor level (computed log k scale back-transformed); get_dd_comparisons() returns pairwise treatment-vs-control contrasts ratios discount rates, multiplicity adjustment via stats::p.adjust method. broom + base S3 surface beezdiscounting_tmb objects: tidy(), glance() (backend "TMB_mixed"), augment(), coef(), fixef(), ranef(), confint(), predict(), summary(), logLik(), AIC(), BIC(), nobs(), print().
